per_query_results.question: What is the primary difference between Full-Reference (FR), Reduced-Reference (RR), and No-Reference (NR) Image Quality Assessment?
per_query_results.target_paper: Comprehensive Survey on Image Quality Assessment
per_query_results.generated_answer: Full-Reference (FR) IQA evaluates distorted images by comparing them directly against a pristine reference image. Reduced-Reference (RR) IQA has access only to partial feature descriptions or statistical summaries of the reference image. No-Reference (NR or blind) IQA predicts visual quality directly from the distorted image without any access to the original reference. [Comprehensive Survey on Image Quality Assessment, Introduction & Taxonomy]

per_query_results.question: How does BRISQUE (Blind/Referenceless Image Spatial Quality Evaluator) compute quality features in the spatial domain?

per_query_results.question: Why is Mean Squared Error (MSE) / PSNR often criticized as a poor metric for human perceptual image quality?

per_query_results.question: How does NIQE (Natural Image Quality Evaluator) differ from BRISQUE in its training methodology?

per_query_results.generated_answer: While BRISQUE is trained using a supervised regression model on both pristine and distorted images with human Mean Opinion Scores (MOS), NIQE is completely unsupervised, constructed solely using a multivariate Gaussian (MVG) model of natural pristine images. Distorted images are scored by computing the distance (Bhattacharyya or Mahalanobis) between their spatial NSS features and the pristine MVG model.
